newsitem.title: USA: Zenith develops HDTV demodulation chips.
newsitem.headline: Zenith develops HDTV demodulation chips.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp said Thursday it has developed what it believes to be the first semiconductors for the digital high-definition (HDTV) terrestrial broadcast transmission system adopted by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission.

It said it is in talks with a variety of chip manufacturers on the "VSB" digital transmission technology and related integrated circuits for HDTV sets. The chips are expected to be available later this year, it noted.
Extensive laboratory testing of first-generation chips shows compatibility with the FCC-approved VSB transmission system, said Paul Snopko, Zenith's research and development director.

"VSB is rugged digital technology for terrestrial braodcasting that assumes a broad HDTV coverage area, reduces interference with existing analog broadcasts and provides immunity from interference into the digital signal," Snopko said in a statement.

The VSB chip-set, fabricated by LG Electronics Inc's LG Semicon, includes two application specific integrated circuits, one for synchronization/equalization and one for channel decoding. LG Electronics is a majority holder in Zenith.

The Zenith VSB digital transmission system was adopted by the FCC in December 1996 as part of the ATSC (Advanced Television Systems Committee) digital television standard developed by Zenith and other members of the Digital HDTV Grand Alliance.
